image_description: A close-up, macro photograph of a tiger beetle facing the camera. The beetle has a metallic reddish-bronze head and thorax with iridescent blue-green highlights on the legs and body edges. It features large compound eyes, prominent white markings on the elytra, and long, slender legs positioned on a mossy green surface. The mandibles are visible but appear somewhat short and blunt rather than distinctly sickle-shaped.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The mandibles lack the precise biological definition of a tiger beetle. They appear slightly melted or fused at the base, lacking the clear separation and sharp sickle curve expected. This is a subtle anatomical error common in AI generation.

The connection points of the legs to the thorax and the antennae to the head show slight softness and lack of crisp chitinous detail, suggesting minor generative smoothing rather than sharp optical focus.
The antennae seem to fade out or distort slightly as they extend, not maintaining a consistent filiform thickness, which may be an artifact of generation or depth handling.
